tip: 'çektirdim' adds -tir- to 'çekmek' so it means I had it pulled, not I pulled. The doer takes -e, here 'dişçiye' (by the dentist).
Adding -ınca to a verb means once or when it happens. 'açınca' is once it opened, said of the sun coming out.
Turkish builds fractions backwards. 'üçte bir' is literally in three, one, which means one third.
When a verb is the object of another verb it takes -meyi. 'gitmeyi planlıyoruz' is we are planning to go.
'gidemeyeceğim' stacks -eme, meaning cannot, onto the future, so it is I will not be able to go.
To say under something, the object takes -ın and 'alt' takes a location ending. 'yatağın altında' is under the bed.
To turn a whole action into a noun, the doer takes -in and the verb takes -ması. 'dedemin kapatması' is my grandfather's closing.
'için' after a plain -mak verb means in order to. 'kutlamak için' is in order to celebrate.
To say because, put -dığı için on the verb. 'uyuyamadığım için' is because I could not sleep.
The suffix -ce on a group means all together as that group. 'ailece' is as a whole family.
For an unreal past, use -mış olsaydı in the if part. 'yatmış olsaydım' is if I had gone to bed.
-mıştım marks an action already finished before another past moment. 'çıkmıştım' is I had already left.
'konuşulur' adds the passive -ul- to 'konuşmak', so it means are spoken with no named speaker.
Put 'en' before an adjective to make the most. 'en çalışkan' is the most hardworking.
-en turns a verb into an adjective sitting before its noun. 'ekilen buğday' is the wheat that was planted.
Add -ıncı to a number to make the ordinal. 'altı' becomes 'altıncı', the sixth.
'göre' after a noun with -e means compared to, and 'daha' marks the comparison. 'şehre göre daha temiz' is cleaner than the city.
'nerede olduğunu' packs where it is into one noun-like clause; the subject 'kütüphanenin' takes -nin.
The -ip on 'düşüp' links it to 'sakatlandı'; only the last verb carries the tense, and both share the subject.
'baksaydık' is the past unreal, if we had looked; the result 'kaybetmezdik' means we wouldn't have lost.
The -la on 'arkadaşlarımla' means with; the suffixes stack as 'arkadaş-lar-ım-la', friends-my-with.
Position words put the owner in -nın: 'masanın altına' means to under the table, with -a marking motion toward.
A negative command adds -ma to the bare verb: 'bırak' means leave, 'bırakma' means don't leave.
The -siz ending means without: 'reçete' is prescription, 'reçetesiz' means without a prescription.
The frame 'ne kadar ... o kadar' means the more ... the more, pairing 'okursan' with 'öğrenirsin'.
-sa plus 'bile' means even if: 'olsa bile' is even if there were, so 'param olsa bile' means even if I had money.
The -dıkça ending means as one does X, the more: 'yaşlandıkça' means as one grows older.
The -laş ending turns an adjective into a 'become' verb: 'zor' is hard, so 'zorlaşıyor' means is getting hard.
Ownership is owner with -nın plus thing with -si plus 'var': 'binanın ... dairesi var' means the building has apartments.
In a passive, the doer is named with 'tarafından', by: 'turist tarafından ziyaret edilir', is visited by tourists.
